title: G-Drive recovers from a penalty to win at Red Bull Ring
dek: Roman Rusinov, Andrea Pizzitola and Jean-Eric Vergne won the 4 Hours of Red Bull Ring from fifth on the grid despite a drive-through, as Duqueine's runner-up place was lost to a fuel exclusion.

chapters.title: A title fight and a fuel-rig ruling
text: The 4 Hours of Red Bull Ring on 22 July 2018 was the third of six European Le Mans Series rounds and the first race after the Le Mans 24 Hours. The LMP2 order was already unsettled. Racing Engineering had won on its series debut at Le Castellet in April with the all-French trio of Olivier Pla, Norman Nato and Paul Petit, and G-Drive Racing's TDS-run Oreca #26 had answered with a dominant win at Monza in May, nearly half a minute clear of the #33 TDS car that had started from the back of the class. G-Drive arrived in Austria as championship leader.

The Le Mans result hung over the paddock. G-Drive's Oreca had been excluded from the LMP2 win at the 24 Hours after the TDS-run cars were found to have used modified fuel rigs, with an extra component fitted to defeat the fill-rate restrictor and save six to eight seconds a stop. The FIA Court of Appeal was not due to rule until September. Ahead of the Austrian weekend the ELMS Committee published its own answer to a team's query, rejecting any added part between the restrictor and the dead-man valve.

Jean-Eric Vergne, fresh from clinching the Formula E title, shared the #26 with Roman Rusinov and Andrea Pizzitola. Nicolas Minassian, IDEC Sport's sporting director, made his first start for the team in the all-gentleman #27 Ligier with Patrice Lafargue and Erik Maris, and the second G-Drive car, the #40, ran as a two-driver crew of James Allen and Jose Gutierrez. Duqueine Engineering, new to LMP2 this year, brought Pierre Ragues, Nicolas Jamin and Nelson Panciatici. Paul Loup Chatin set the pace in both practice sessions for IDEC Sport, the second of them in heavy rain that caused two Full Course Yellows, with the #26 and the Racing Engineering car in second and third.

chapters.title: Chatin snatches pole after the flag
text: Paul Loup Chatin took pole for IDEC Sport with a 1:19.246 in the #28 Oreca, set on his seventh lap after the chequered flag had fallen. Nicolas Jamin had led most of the session for Duqueine Engineering and was bumped to second by just 0.019 seconds. Chatin described a lap on the limit after a traffic-filled start to the session, with two fresh tyres giving him the extra laps to chase the time.

Norman Nato was third for Racing Engineering on 1:19.387, ahead of Nicolas Lapierre's DragonSpeed car and the #26, in which Pizzitola set the fifth-fastest time, and Loic Duval in the #33 TDS entry. Orecas filled the first six places. Filipe Albuquerque was the best of the Ligier JS P217s in seventh for United Autosports, while Felipe Nasr led the Dallara P217s in tenth for Cetilar Villorba Corse, and the top ten were covered by less than a second. The only notable incident came when Anders Fjordbach's High Class Racing Dallara lost a front-right wheel leaving the pits, though it was recovered without a Full Course Yellow.

In the other classes, JMW Motorsport's Miguel Molina put the first Ferrari pole of the season on the GTE front, 0.098 seconds ahead of the #88 Porsche, and in LMP3 AT Racing's provisional pole was taken away for track limits, handing it to the Ultimate Norma. The overall grid read #28 IDEC, #29 Duqueine, #24 Racing Engineering, with Rusinov due to start the winning car from fifth.

chapters.title: Ragues pounces, Rusinov jumps
text: The race started at noon in changeable conditions, with a series of short showers expected to shape the afternoon. Pierre Ragues passed the pole-sitting IDEC Oreca of Paul Lafargue at Turn 1 and pulled away with ease, while Rusinov wasted little time in getting the #26 onto the back of the IDEC car. That ended when the stewards handed him a drive-through penalty for jumping the start.

The penalty dropped the G-Drive car well down the order and forced the team onto an alternative strategy. Rusinov later called it probably the best thing that could have happened to them, because the engineers had to find a new plan and that plan won the race.

chapters.title: Contact, yellows and rain
text: The first round of stops brought driver changes up and down the order: Jamin took over the Duqueine from Ragues, Nato replaced Petit in the Racing Engineering car and Memo Rojas took over the IDEC Oreca. Nato quickly closed on Rojas and passed him on lap 66 at Turn 4. Moments later Rojas, Konstantin Tereschenko's AVF by Adrian Valles Dallara #30 and an Oregon Team LMP3 car made contact. The IDEC Oreca needed front bodywork repairs.

The incident brought a Full Course Yellow, and all the leaders pitted under it except Nato in the #24. He later called it one small mistake that cost the team the win. Pizzitola, who drove a triple stint, used the neutralisations to climb back into the top three, and Vergne took over on lap 92 and quickly became the fastest car on the track. Rain arrived around half-distance in short, sometimes sharp bursts, though never enough to bring wet tyres, and the greasier surface helped Dunlop-shod cars close on the Michelin-shod Duqueine. By the end of the third hour the #26 had edged ahead of the Duqueine on strategy, which had led most of the way and at times by a big margin.

chapters.title: Vergne holds on with a splash
text: With roughly half an hour left Panciatici came in for the Duqueine's final stop and Vergne inherited a clean lead. The #26 still needed a splash of fuel to reach the flag, and was called in with ten minutes to go; the stop was so brief that Vergne rejoined still in front. He crossed the line after 160 laps and 4:00:14.242 of racing, just under 20 seconds ahead of Panciatici.

Behind them the fight for second was far tighter. Olivier Pla moved into the top three when Chatin pitted the IDEC car with a quarter of an hour remaining, then sat on the Duqueine's tail and tried a bold move around the outside at the Remus hairpin with eight minutes left. It did not stick, and Panciatici held on by two tenths. Phil Hanson and Filipe Albuquerque finished fourth on the road in the #22 Ligier, more than half a minute further back, having fought a damaged rear end all race, while Chatin's IDEC car emerged from its late fuel stop in fifth. The finishing order was provisional.

chapters.title: Fuel exclusion for Duqueine
text: Late on Sunday the ELMS stewards excluded the #29 Duqueine Engineering Oreca, citing a post-race fuel sample that did not conform to the one indicated by the organiser (Stewards' Decision 35). Panciatici, Ragues and Jamin lost their runner-up result, which promoted Racing Engineering's Pla, Nato and Petit to second, 20.126 seconds behind the winners, and put United Autosports' Hanson and Albuquerque on the podium in third, 54.166 seconds back. IDEC Sport's Lafargue, Chatin and Rojas finished fourth, delayed by the mid-race contact.

Duqueine team manager Yann Belhomme explained the cause the next day. A small amount of ELF fuel was left over from the Cool Racing LMP3 Norma that had run at the Road to Le Mans, and had been used during a private test at the Red Bull Ring the previous Wednesday. Some stayed in the bottom of the tank after it was emptied between runs, and the sample showed that around 0.5 percent came from the test mix. ELF and the Total fuel used on all ELMS rounds share the same 102 grade, which is why the mix was possible in the Oreca. Belhomme said he totally accepted the decision, apologised to the drivers and to Michelin and sponsors, and added that the team had fought for first place in qualifying and the race.

For G-Drive it was a second successive win in the series and it extended the Rusinov, Pizzitola and Vergne crew's lead in the LMP2 points, with the Le Mans fuel-rig question still awaiting the September appeal. Pizzitola's triple stint, the neutralisations and Vergne's anchor leg had turned a start-line penalty into a winning strategy, while for Nato the decision to stay out under the yellow stood as the near-miss of the day.

United's Ligier was the best of the non-Oreca chassis, and IDEC Sport, whose pole-sitter had faded after the contact, was due to field Aurelien Panis in the #27 car at the next round. The ELMS next visits Silverstone on 18 August for the 4 Hours of Silverstone, and Duqueine said it hoped to be back on the top step there.

facts.v: Paul Loup Chatin took pole in the IDEC Sport Oreca #28 with a 1:19.246, set after the flag, just 0.019 seconds ahead of Nicolas Jamin's Duqueine.
Rusinov jumped the start and took a drive-through, yet the #26 G-Drive Oreca came back to win by just under 20 seconds on the road.
The ELMS Committee rejected any part between the restrictor and the dead-man valve, weeks after the TDS-run Orecas were excluded from the Le Mans LMP2 win.
The #29 Duqueine Oreca lost second place after a fuel sample did not conform, promoting Racing Engineering to second and United's #22 to third.

facts.t: Test fuel left in the tank
facts.v: Duqueine said ELF fuel from a Cool Racing Norma used in a private test remained in the Oreca; the sample showed about 0.5 percent of it.
